title: djLint configuration
description: Configuration for djLint, an HTML template linter and formatter. https://djlint.com/docs/configuration/

$schema.description: The url of the schema this file is checked against.

allow_empty_input.description: Exit with 0 instead of 2 when the given paths match no files at all. Files that were found and then skipped by `exclude`, `extend_exclude`, `use_gitignore` or `require_pragma` already exit with 0.

blank_line_after_tag.description: Template tags to follow with a blank line, such as `load` and `extends`. A group of them in a row gets one after the last, and none is added at the end of a block.

blank_line_before_tag.description: Template tags to precede with a blank line, such as `load` and `extends`. A group of them in a row gets one before the first, and none is added at the start of a file or block.

close_void_tags.description: Close known void tags with a slash, so `` becomes ``. `H018`, which asks for the opposite, is not reported under it.

css.description: Options passed to cssbeautifier when --format-css is on, such as indent_size.

custom_blocks.description: Names of custom template blocks to indent, such as `toc` for `{% toc %}...{% endtoc %}`.

custom_html.description: Names of custom HTML tags to indent, such as `mjml` or `simple-greeting`. A name can be a regex, as in `mj-\w+`.

exclude.description: Paths to skip, in place of the default list. Each entry is a regular expression matched against whole folder or file names in the path relative to the project root, such as `vendor` or `templates/legacy`, so `*.min.html` is written `.*\.min\.html`.

extend_exclude.description: Paths to skip on top of the default list, as regular expressions like those of `exclude`.

extension.description: Extension of the files to look for in folders. It takes one extension; a file given by name is checked whatever its extension.

files.description: Paths to check instead of the ones on the command line, which must then be `-`, as for stdin. With `--stdin-filename`, `-` means stdin regardless.

format_attribute_js_json.description: Also format JavaScript and JSON in attributes such as `onclick` and `x-data`, the ones `format_attribute_js_json_pattern` names. An object with fewer properties than `format_attribute_js_json_min_props` stays on one line.

format_attribute_js_json_min_props.description: Format an object only when it has at least this many properties. One with fewer stays on one line.

format_attribute_js_json_pattern.description: Regex for the names of the attributes to format as JavaScript or JSON. The default takes `on*` event handlers and the bindings of Alpine, Vue, Angular and Aurelia.

format_attribute_template_tags.description: Format template syntax inside tag attributes.

format_css.description:
Also format the contents of `<style>` tags, with [css-beautify](https://github.com/beautify-web/js-beautify). Template syntax inside them is not fully supported.

`indent_size` in the `css` table, or `--indent-css` on the command line, sets the indent inside `<style>` tags, 4 by default. The table takes the other [css-beautify options](https://github.com/beautify-web/js-beautify/blob/main/python/cssbeautifier/css/options.py) too.

format_js.description:
Also format JavaScript and JSON in `<script>` tags, with [js-beautify](https://github.com/beautify-web/js-beautify). A script whose `type` is neither JavaScript nor JSON, such as a client-side template in `text/template`, is left as written. Template syntax inside them is not fully supported.

`indent_size` in the `js` table, or `--indent-js` on the command line, sets the indent inside `<script>` tags, 4 by default. The table takes the other [js-beautify options](https://github.com/beautify-web/js-beautify/blob/main/python/jsbeautifier/javascript/options.py) too.

ignore_blocks.description: Template blocks that do not indent their contents. Their children are treated as siblings of the block and indented accordingly.

ignore_case.description: Do not fix the case of known HTML tags. `H009` and `H010` are not reported under it.

include.description: Linter codes to turn on that are off by default or that the profile leaves out.

indent.description: Spaces per indent level. When it isn't set, djLint takes the `indent_size` that `.editorconfig` gives the file, if any.

js.description: Options passed to jsbeautifier when --format-js is on, such as indent_size.

keep_br_inline.description:
Keep `
` on the line of the text it breaks, rather than giving it a line of its own. `
`, which renders as a rule below the preceding content, is unaffected.

line_break_after_multiline_tag.description: When a tag's attributes are spread over lines, start its content on a new line.

linter_output_format.description: The layout of each lint message, from `{filename}`, `{line}`, `{end}`, `{code}`, `{message}` and `{match}`. Without `{filename}`, the output is grouped by file and each group gets a header.

max_attribute_length.description: The formatter spreads a tag's attributes over lines once they are longer than this.

max_blank_lines.description: Keep at most this many blank lines in a row, so 0 removes them. It has no effect with `preserve_blank_lines`.

max_line_length.description: The formatter joins some HTML and template tags onto one line only when the line fits within this length. When it isn't set, djLint takes the `max_line_length` that `.editorconfig` gives the file, if any.

name_endblocks.description: Write the block's name into the `{% endblock %}` that closes it, where the block is written across lines. This is what `T003` asks for.

no_entity_formatting.description: Do not rewrite an entity reference as the character it names, so `©` is left as written rather than becoming `©`. The entities that carry syntax, and the invisible ones, are never rewritten either way. `H023` still reports an entity under it; add `H023` to `ignore` to keep entities.

no_function_formatting.description: Do not format the arguments of function calls inside `{{ }}`.

no_indent_inner_html.description: Do not indent `<head>` and `<body>` inside `<html>`, which is how the built-in VS Code HTML formatter lays a document out.

no_line_after_yaml.description: Do not add a blank line after YAML front matter.

no_set_formatting.description: Do not format the contents of `{% set %}` tags.

per-file-ignores.description: Linter codes to skip in the files whose path matches a regex. In a config file the key is `per-file-ignores`, with hyphens.

preserve_blank_lines.description: Keep blank lines where possible. Useful for templates other than HTML, where blank lines are intentional.

preserve_class_newlines.description: Keep the line breaks in `class` attributes written across lines.

preserve_leading_space.description: Keep the leading spaces of text lines where possible. Useful for templates other than HTML, where the indent of text is intentional.

profile.description:
The template language. It decides which linter rules run and how the template syntax is formatted: in `handlebars`, for example, there are no spaces inside `{{#if}}` tags.

Without a profile, djLint formats the template syntax of every language, as `all` does, and lints with the rules of `html`.

Options:

- html
- django
- jinja
- nunjucks (for nunjucks and twig)
- handlebars (for handlebars and mustache)
- liquid (shopify, jekyll, eleventy)
- golang (go templates; hugo, helm)
- angular
- tera (also for zola; use jinja for minijinja)
- askama (jinja-style templates in rust; rust expressions are never reformatted)
- mako (control lines and `##` comments are kept as written)
- all (every template language at once)

quiet.description: Do not print diffs, the progress bar or the summary.

quote_style.description: Quotes for strings inside template tags, `double` or `single`. `T002` asks for the same quotes, and the formatter uses them in conditions such as `{% if x == "a" %}`, so one file does not spell the same string both ways. Quoting of HTML attributes is left to `H008`.

single_attribute_per_line.description: When an opening tag wraps, put the tag name, each attribute and the closing bracket on separate lines.

sort_attributes.description: Sort attributes by name, with `id` first and `class` second. A tag whose attributes are guarded by a template tag keeps the order it was written in, since moving one out of its branch would change the page.

sort_load_tags.description: Sort the libraries in `{% load %}` tags and drop the ones written twice, so `{% load static i18n %}` becomes `{% load i18n static %}`. In `{% load a b from library %}` the names before `from` are sorted. Where two libraries define a tag or filter of the same name, the one loaded last wins, so sorting can change which one the template uses.

use_gitignore.description: Also skip the paths that the `.gitignore` in the project root lists.
